careers.introTemplate: Global Health connects patients in {country} with registered doctors online. Behind every consultation is a team of clinicians, clinical-operations staff and engineers working across our markets — and we are always glad to hear from people who want to join them.
careers.heroImageAlt: Doctors and care team working at Global Health
careers.trustRemoteSubtitle: Work from anywhere in our markets
careers.whyHeading: Work that reaches patients in six countries
careers.whyBodyTemplate: We keep the team small and the standards high. Whether you consult with patients, support them around a booking, or build the platform itself, your work goes live for patients in {country} and across every market we operate in.
careers.pillarDoctorsBody: Consult online with the national medical register behind you. You set your availability; we handle bookings, payments and the technology around the consultation.
careers.pillarOpsBody: Help patients before and after their consultation — bookings, documents, follow-ups — in the languages our markets speak.
careers.pillarTechBody: Build the platform that delivers regulated healthcare online: booking, records, prescriptions and everything between, across six countries.
careers.rolesBody: We do not list vacancies on this page. If you are a registered doctor, a clinical-support professional or an engineer and want to work with us, send your CV and a few lines about yourself — we read every application and reply to those we can take further.

medicalReview.descriptionTemplate: How Global Health writes, reviews and updates the health articles published for {country}: who writes them, which registered physician signs them off, and the editorial standards we hold ourselves to.
medicalReview.h1: How we write and review medical content
medicalReview.introTemplate: Every clinical article we publish for {country} is drafted from primary sources, checked against them, and signed off by a named physician registered with {regulator} before it reaches you — and reviewed again when the underlying rules change.
medicalReview.heroImageAlt: Global Health editorial and clinical review policy
medicalReview.trustNamedSubtitle: Clinical sign-off by a named, registered doctor
medicalReview.trustSourcedSubtitle: Rules link to the body that sets them
medicalReview.trustCurrentSubtitle: Re-reviewed at least once a year
medicalReview.s1Body1: Articles begin as a draft built from verified primary sources — government guidance, national health authority publications, and the social security or insurance body documentation that applies in the country the article is written for. Drafting may involve editorial tools, but no article is published on the strength of a tool alone.
medicalReview.s1Body2Template: Articles carry one editorial byline — the Global Health Medical Team — because drafting, sourcing and editing are a team effort rather than one person's work. Clinical accountability is not anonymous, though: a physician registered with {regulator} signs the article off, and it is their name and registration number that appear on it.
medicalReview.s2Heading: Who reviews it, and what they check
medicalReview.s2Intro: Before publication, the article is reviewed in full by a registered physician. This is not a formality: the reviewer is expected to check claims against the source material rather than simply approve the draft. That physician is named on the article, with the registration number that lets you check them yourself.
medicalReview.s2AuthorBody: Every article is drafted, sourced and edited by our clinical editorial team, so it carries one consistent byline rather than rotating individual names.
medicalReview.s2ReviewerBody: A registered physician checks the article before publication, and again whenever it is materially updated. Their name and registration are published on the article.
medicalReview.s2BylineIntro: The article names the physician who signed it off, with a registration you can check yourself. A published byline reads like this:
medicalReview.s2BylineFormatNote: The reviewer name and registration number on our articles belong to a doctor on the public register for this market — never a placeholder.
medicalReview.s3Heading: Editorial standards we hold ourselves to
medicalReview.s3Std1Title: Figures and thresholds are never hard-coded.
medicalReview.s3Std1Body: Amounts, waiting periods and eligibility rules set by government or insurance bodies change over time. Where an article would otherwise state one, it links to the issuing body's own page instead, so you always see the current figure.
medicalReview.s3Std2Title: Every regulatory claim links to its source.
medicalReview.s3Std2Body: Statements about entitlements, certification rules or legal processes link directly to the government department, health authority or regulator that defines them — not to a summary of a summary.
medicalReview.s3Std3Title: Country-specific rules are written for that country.
medicalReview.s3Std3BodyTemplate: An article about sick leave in {country} is written and reviewed for {country}, separately from the same topic in another market, because the rules genuinely differ.
medicalReview.s3Std4Title: Nothing here replaces an individual assessment.
medicalReview.s3Std4Body: Articles explain how a process generally works. They do not diagnose, and they do not guarantee a specific outcome in your case — that requires an actual consultation.
medicalReview.s3Std5BodyTemplate: Where an article mentions warning signs that warrant urgent care, it gives the emergency number that applies in this market — {emergency}.
medicalReview.s4Body1: Regulatory content is reviewed at least once a year, or sooner if we become aware that a rule, form or process it describes has changed. Where an article has been clinically reviewed, the date of that review is shown on the article, so you can judge how current it is at a glance.
medicalReview.s4Body2: If a review results in a material change to the guidance, the reviewing physician's name and the review date are updated with it.
medicalReview.s5Body: Tell us. Every report is checked by a member of our clinical team, and corrections are made publicly and promptly.
medicalReview.footerNote: This policy describes the editorial process for the general health information published on this site. It does not apply to personalised medical advice given during a consultation, which follows separate clinical governance standards.
